4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.

8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.

12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies

17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart

20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:

38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens

46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is an irreducible L_K-module. This holds including λ=0 and p=2 and without any algebraic-closure assumption on K.

value.representation_notes: Use the actual complex representation via its three complex-linear Chevalley operators; their commutator relations specify an sl2 action. p is natural because every integer prime in the source is positive; ell remains an integer and ell.toNat is used only under H001's 0≤ell. Index ell=Fin(ell.toNat+1) is the endpoint-inclusive source I via i↦(i.val:ℤ). M is a Z-submodule of V, equivalent to an additive subgroup. The rational localization R is the Z-subalgebra of Q generated by reciprocals of all integers not divisible by p; T005 proves its precise fraction description rather than assuming it. Tensor products are left scalar extensions R⊗Z M and K⊗Z M. mu is scalar multiplication, and J is the exact coordinate inverse image of its range. qmul is the actual multiplication map into C, never an abstract rank surrogate. The endomorphism restriction latticeOp is defined by restriction when preservation holds and zero otherwise; T005 proves preservation so all operators used in the theorem are the genuine induced lattice maps. Library instance constructors in definitions provide only canonical scalar restrictions. They assert no unproved mathematical properties.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: For the optional [basis route](../../nl0/references/basis.md), this same Audit B
4: checks the conditional intermediate under the frozen basis interfaces. It is
5: followed by b2lean's fresh inspection of the actual `YuiClosed.P`, with only
6: original H and explicitly approved class 4 remaining. Its final receipt binds
7: the compiled standalone source and full actual signature/dependency closure;
8: this intermediate receipt must not be reported as unconditional completion.
9: 
10: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
11: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
12: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
13: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
14: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
15: 
16: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
17: 
18: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
19: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
20: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
21: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
22: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
23: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
24: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
25: 
26: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
27: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
28: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
29: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
30: 
31: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
32: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
33: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
34: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
35: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
36: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
37: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
38: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
39: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
40: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
41: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
42: 
43: ## Author correspondence explanations
44: 
45: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
46: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
47: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
48: line-by-line formalization commentary:
49: 
50: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
51:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
52: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
53:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
54:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
55: 
56: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
57: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
58: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
59: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
60: 
61: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
62: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
63: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
64: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
65: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
66: 
67: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
68: 
69: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
70: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
71: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
72: row, then these four global checks:
73: 
74: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
75:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
76: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
77:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
78:    no external inputs, record that fact.
79: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
80:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
81:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
82: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
83:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
84:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
85: 
86: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
87: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
88: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
89: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
90: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
91: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
92: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
93: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
94: 
95: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
96: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
97: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
98: 
99: ## Freely available Mathlib
100: 
101: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
102: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
103: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
104: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
105: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
106: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
107: permissions to use a library theorem.
108: 
109: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
110: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
111: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
112: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
113: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
114: require returning to the affected source boundary.
115: 
116: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
117: 
118: ### Compact review materials
119: 
120: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
121: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
122: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
123: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
124: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
125: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
126: expected type for the actual inspected type.
127: 
128: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
129: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
130: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
131: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
132: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
133: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
134: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
135: 
136: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
137: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
138: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
139: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
140: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
141: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
142: 
143: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
144: 
145: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
146: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
147: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
148: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
149: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
150: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
151: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
152: 
153: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
154: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
155: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
156: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
157: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
158: 
159: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
160: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
161: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
162: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
163: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
164: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
165: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
166: 
167: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
168: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
169: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
170: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
171: review have separate recorded outcomes.
172: 
173: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
174: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
175: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
176: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
177: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
178: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
179: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
180: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
181: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
182: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

namespace Chevalley
def R (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance rComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  Algebra.compHom ℂ (algebraMap (R p) ℚ)
variable {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
def dp (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (R p) ⊗[ℤ] M
def mu (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M → V :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def image (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Set V := Set.range (mu p M)
def latticeOp (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  letI := Classical.propDecidable
  if hf : ∀ u ∈ M, f u ∈ M then (f.restrictScalars ℤ).restrict hf else 0
abbrev VK (K : Type) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def opK (K : Type) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) :
    Module.End K (VK K M) := (latticeOp M f).baseChange K
def unitOp {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {ι : Type} (b : Module.Basis ι F W) (i j : ι) : Module.End F W :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def muR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
    MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  (muR p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[R p] ℂ) (e y v i))
def QJ (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    Submodule ℚ ℂ := Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v 0 : Set ℂ)
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    ℚ ⊗[R p] (J p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  letI := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℚ ℂ
  (J p M y v 0).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ
abbrev Index (ell : ℤ) := Fin (ell.toNat + 1)
def stable {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (U : Submodule F W) (f : Module.End F W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def inImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ image p M, f w ∈ image p M
def preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ M, f w ∈ M
def reductions (K : Type) [Field K] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ hc : CharP K p,
  letI := hc
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ ρ : R p →+* K,
  (∀ a : ℤ, ρ (a : R p) = (a : K)) ∧
  letI := ρ.toAlgebra
  ∃ Φ : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Φ (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] ((1 : R p) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    ∃ Ψ : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p),
      ∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Ψ (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u
def basisVec {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < n then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def stringActions {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (ell : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End F W) (a : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ ell.toNat →
    x (a i) = (if i = 0 then 0 else ((ell - (i : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • a (i - 1)) ∧
    y (a i) = (if i < ell.toNat then ((i + 1 : ℕ) : F) • a (i + 1) else 0) ∧
    h (a i) = ((ell - 2 * (i : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • a i
def dividedActions {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (ell : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F W) (a : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r i : ℕ), i ≤ ell.toNat →
    X r (a i) = (if r ≤ i then ((Nat.choose (ell.toNat - i + r) r : ℕ) : F) • a (i - r) else 0) ∧
    Y r (a i) = (if i + r ≤ ell.toNat then ((Nat.choose (i + r) r : ℕ) : F) • a (i + r) else 0)
def matrixK (K : Type) [Field K] (ell : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (i j : Index ell) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  ((Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹) •
    (opK K M (dp x (ell.toNat - i.val)) *
      (opK K M (dp y ell.toNat) * opK K M (dp x ell.toNat)) *
        opK K M (dp y (ell.toNat - j.val)))
end Chevalley

value.statement: Let A be a commutative semiring, S a submonoid of A, C0 a commutative A-algebra which is a localization of A at S, B an additive commutative monoid and A-module, B1 an additive commutative monoid with A- and C0-module structures forming a scalar tower, and f:B→B1 an A-linear map. Then IsLocalizedModule(S,f) if and only if IsBaseChange(C0,f). The first predicate says: each s∈S acts invertibly on B1; for each z∈B1 there exist b∈B and s∈S with s z=f(b); and f(b)=f(b') implies s b=s b' for some s∈S. The second predicate says that the canonical C0-linear tensor map C0⊗_A B→B1, c⊗b↦c f(b), is bijective (and thus a linear isomorphism).

value.statement: n=λ+1>0, |I|=n, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V, so dim_C V=n. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Moreover y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher lowering powers vanish. On the basis: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤λ; ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ; ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} when r≤i and zero when r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix entries are integers.

μ:M_R→V is injective and identifies M_R with an R-submodule of V which is free of rank n, spans V over C, and is preserved by every X_r and Y_r (r≥0). For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and P0=E_{λλ}, X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}, P0 Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0 Y_{λ−j}. Consequently every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The operators x,y,h preserve M and hence act on V_K and the localized module.

All modules J_i (i∈I) equal J. The R-module J⊂C is nonzero and finitely generated, and μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I} J e_i internally in V. The multiplication map Q⊗_R J→QJ⊂C, q⊗c↦qc, is injective and surjective onto QJ. With r=dim_Q(Q⊗_R J), r is finite and dim_Q(Q⊗_R M_R)=n=n r; hence r=1 and dim_Q QJ=1.

binders.type: natural number defined here as dim_Q(Q⊗_R J)

value.statement: There exists b∈J with b≠0 such that J=Rb and μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I} R(b e_i). The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of μ(M_R), equivalently its unique μ-preimage is an R-basis of M_R.

There is a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of V_K of cardinality n=λ+1>0 with xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i, all integer coefficients mapped to K. The natural maps give M⊗_Z K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K. For 0≤r≤λ, the induced divided powers are X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r, where r! is nonzero in K. For all i,j∈I, writing P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K, the K-linear operator T_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K satisfies T_ij β_k=β_i if k=j and zero otherwise. Every coefficient inverse in this formula exists in K. Therefore every K-subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under all T_ij.

value.text: H001 gives n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We first prove the commutator formulas for all nonnegative powers. For h, the case t=0 is hv=λv from H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v. Using [h,y]=−2y from H002, h y^{t+1}v=y h y^t v−2y^{t+1}v=(λ−2(t+1))y^{t+1}v. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction proves the h formula for every t≥0. For x, the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=λv by H002 and H003. For t≥1 temporarily assume L2: xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. Discharging L2 proves the step, and induction gives the x formula for all t≥1. These identities are F001.

For i∈I, iterating F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the product is 1 and this is v. All factors for i>0 are positive integers, and v≠0 by H003, so every e_i is nonzero over C. By F001, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i; these eigenvalues are distinct over C. To check independence, fix arbitrary coefficients c=(c_i)_{i∈I} and temporarily assume L3: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id) to this relation. It yields c_j∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0. The product, including an empty product, is nonzero, and e_j≠0, hence c_j=0. Discharge L3 to obtain independence. H002 gives dim_C V=n, and there are n independent e_i, so they form a complex basis. This proves F002.

F001 specialized to exponent λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if it is nonzero. Temporarily assume L4 that it is nonzero. Expanding it in the basis F002, the equality h y^{λ+1}v=(−λ−2)y^{λ+1}v forces every coefficient to vanish: for i∈I, (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i) is a nonzero complex scalar. This is a contradiction, so discharge L4 to conclude y^{λ+1}v=0. Applying further y powers gives all higher vanishing. F001 divided by i!, together with this termination and xv=0 from H003, gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. This proves F003.

Iterate the displayed x,y matrices in F003 and divide by r!. For each natural r and i∈I with r≤i, x^r e_i/r!=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r}. If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed by x. For i+r≤λ, y^r e_i/r!=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r}; otherwise it passes the last vector and is zero. For r=0 the empty products are 1. These are precisely X_r,Y_r by definition. The displayed binomial coefficients, with nonnegative integer upper argument at least r, are integers. Together with F001–F003 this is every assertion of the asserted conclusion.

H004 gives an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. By N001, dim_C V=n and |I|=n. Equality of the cardinalities of finite bases permits reindexing the given lattice basis by I. Thus there exists a family m=(m_i)_{i∈I} which is simultaneously a Z-basis of M and a complex basis of V. This is F001.

Choose such a family m using F001. Since R is a commutative Z-algebra, M001 with A=Z, B=M, C0=R and d=m gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Its image under μ is the family m_i in V. A relation in its kernel is a finite R-linear relation among the complex-independent m_i, so all coefficients are zero. Thus μ is injective; the image is free of rank n and spans V over C. By H004, all X_r,Y_r preserve M, so their scalar extensions preserve M_R and μ intertwines them. Also x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=xy−yx preserves M because H002 gives [x,y]=h. This proves h-stability. Record F002: μ is injective with the claimed free, spanning and stability properties.

For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.

Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. In fraction language a zero image forces a zero numerator, since J⊂C is torsion-free. Define T_Q=Q⊗_R J and r=dim_Q T_Q. The isomorphism and F002 show this dimension is finite. Record F003.

Set A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R. Instantiate the coordinate and insertion maps of F001, denoting them α_i and τ_i. Their scalar extensions give a Q-linear map A_Q→(T_Q)^I sending q⊗u to (q⊗α_i(u))_{i∈I}. Its inverse sends a tuple (z_i) to ∑_{i∈I}(1⊗τ_i)(z_i); here 1⊗τ_i denotes the tensor map q⊗c↦q⊗τ_i(c). These maps are well-defined by R-balancing. The equalities α_iτ_j=δ_ij Id and ∑τ_iα_i=Id in F001 verify the two composite identities, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus A_Q≅(T_Q)^I as Q-vector spaces. This proves F004.

N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R with n elements. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R and C0=Q to this basis: its scalar extension is a Q-basis of A_Q with n elements, so dim_Q A_Q=n. Apply M003 with A=Q, index type I and constant module family T_Q. The field Q satisfies the strong rank condition by finite-dimensional linear algebra; I is finite with n elements by N001. By F003 each T_Q is finite-dimensional, hence free and finitely generated over Q. M003 gives dim_Q((T_Q)^I)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. F004 therefore gives n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, cancellation in the natural numbers yields r=1. F003 now gives dim_Q QJ=1, while F001 gives the finite generation, nonzero property and decomposition. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

Choose 0≠a∈J using N003. N003 identifies Q⊗_R J with the one-dimensional subspace QJ⊂C. Since a≠0, a is a Q-basis of that line. Take finite generators of J, discard any zero generators, and use J≠0 to see the remaining list is nonempty. Every remaining generator is a nonzero rational multiple of a. Therefore there exist k≥1 and q_1,…,q_k∈Q\{0} such that J is generated over R by q_1a,…,q_ka. This is F001.

Choose k,q as in F001. For each 1≤j≤k, write q_j as a ratio of nonzero integers, remove the maximal powers of the prime p from numerator and denominator, and define ν_j to be the difference of these two exponents. Then q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a rational whose numerator and denominator are both prime to p. Such u_j and its reciprocal belong to R, so u_j is a unit. This construction also covers negative ν_j. Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j and b=p^ν a. The minimum exists and is attained because k≥1 and the list is finite. All q_j a belong to Rb, since q_j a=p^{ν_j−ν}u_j b and ν_j−ν≥0. Also b≠0, since p is prime by H001 and a≠0. Record F002, including the existence of a minimizing index.

Choose a minimizing index j0 from F002. Then q_{j0}a=u_{j0}b, and u_{j0} is an R-unit. Since q_{j0}a is a generator of J by F001, b=u_{j0}^{−1}q_{j0}a belongs to J and Rb⊆J. The reverse inclusion follows from F001 and the inclusion of every generator in Rb from F002. Thus J=Rb with b∈J nonzero. This is F003.

Substitute F003 in the direct decomposition of N003 to obtain μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}R(b e_i). The vectors b e_i are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex-independent by N001. They span by the displayed decomposition, so are an R-basis. Since μ is injective by N002, their unique preimages form an R-basis of M_R. Existentially quantify b to prove the asserted conclusion. In particular no rank-one claim has been inferred from containment in C alone.

H001 implies that every integer denominator prime to p maps to a nonzero element of K. Define ρ:R→K by ρ(a/b)=a_K b_K^{−1}. Cross multiplication makes this well-defined and a ring homomorphism extending Z→K. There is also the injective prime-field map F_p→K. Define Φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by Φ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c; its inverse is (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c. Both formulas respect the tensor relations (the R-action on K is through ρ), and the composites are identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Next define the map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K by u⊗c↦(u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends a residue tensor (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: replacing u by u+pt changes this by pt⊗c=t⊗pc=0. It is balanced over F_p, and its R-balancing is justified by R/pR≅F_p, explicitly a/b mod p↦a_p b_p^{-1}; the kernel is pR and every residue is obtained from an integer. These maps are inverse on generators. All maps commute with operators induced from M or M_R, by their formulas. Such x,y,h and divided powers exist by N002. This proves the natural identifications in F001.

Choose b as in N004. For each i∈I define m_i to be the unique μ-preimage of b e_i; N002 gives injectivity and N004 gives membership and the R-basis property of this family in M_R. Define β_i=Φ^{-1}(m_i⊗1)∈V_K. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R, C0=K, the algebra structure ρ and the R-basis (m_i). It gives the K-basis (1⊗m_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The factor-switching isomorphism c⊗u↦u⊗c (with inverse u⊗c↦c⊗u), followed by Φ^{-1}, gives the K-basis β. It has |I|=n=λ+1>0 elements by N001. Because μ intertwines the divided powers, and b is a common complex scalar, the matrices on m_i are exactly those on e_i from N001. F001 carries these matrices to V_K with every integer entry mapped into K. Thus xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The divided-power matrices also descend: X_r^K β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_{i−r} for r≤i, zero for r>i, and Y_r^K β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ, zero otherwise. Here X_r^K,Y_r^K denote the operators induced from X_r,Y_r on M_R. Record F002.

N002 gives, inside the localized lattice, E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}, with P0=Y_λX_λ, and says all these factors preserve it. In the basis (b e_i), E_ij has a single entry 1 in position (i,j), the same as in (e_i). Scalar extension through F001 therefore carries the equality to the operator T_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)^{-1})X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K on β, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K. It satisfies T_ijβ_k=β_i for k=j and 0 for k≠j. Since binom(λ,j) is a unit of R by N002, its image is a unit of K (ρ sends its inverse to an inverse). Also for 0≤r≤λ<p, no factor of r! is divisible by p by H001, so r! maps to a nonzero element of K. The equalities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold over C by definition, hence on M_R by injectivity of μ, and after scalar extension. Consequently X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. This proves F003.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x and y. Induction on the power shows it is invariant under x^r and y^r for every natural r. Because W is K-linear it is stable under scalar multiples and compositions of its preserving operators. F003 expresses all X_r^K,Y_r^K for r≤λ as scalar multiples of these powers, and T_ij as a scalar times a composition of these operators, since λ−i,λ,λ−j are all in [0,λ]. Therefore W is invariant under every T_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with F001–F003, existentially quantify the compatible basis β to obtain the asserted conclusion.

Choose a basis β and the compatible matrix operators guaranteed by N005. This basis has n=λ+1>0 elements, so dim_K V_K=n>0 and V_K≠0; record this as F001. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is x,y-invariant, and N005 says it is invariant under every T_ij. By classical cases, either W={0}, which is already one required alternative, or temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. Under L1,L2, a nonzero vector in W has a unique expansion in the basis β; at least one coefficient is nonzero, since a vector with every coefficient zero is zero. Thus there exist w∈W, a coefficient family c:I→K, and j∈I with w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i≠0 and c_j≠0. This is F002 under L1,L2.

Choose w,c,j as in F002. For every i∈I, linearity and the matrix-unit action in N005 give T_ij w=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiply by c_j^{-1} to get β_i∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine this result with the W={0} case to obtain W={0} or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 to get the implication for this arbitrary W, then universally quantify W. This gives F003 with no remaining local assumptions.

F001 proves nonzero dimension and F003 proves exactly the required subspace assertion. L_K is spanned over K by the three induced generators x,y,h, so a K-linear subspace is L_K-invariant exactly when it is invariant under those three operators. value.statement: Let A be a commutative semiring, S a submonoid of A, C0 a commutative A-algebra which is a localization of A at S, B an additive commutative monoid and A-module, B1 an additive commutative monoid with A- and C0-module structures forming a scalar tower, and f:B→B1 an A-linear map. Then IsLocalizedModule(S,f) if and only if IsBaseChange(C0,f). The first predicate says: each s∈S acts invertibly on B1; for each z∈B1 there exist b∈B and s∈S with s z=f(b); and f(b)=f(b') implies s b=s b' for some s∈S. The second predicate says that the canonical C0-linear tensor map C0⊗_A B→B1, c⊗b↦c f(b), is bijective (and thus a linear isomorphism).

134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.

argument.text: H001 gives n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We first prove the commutator formulas for all nonnegative powers. For h, the case t=0 is hv=λv from H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v. Using [h,y]=−2y from H002, h y^{t+1}v=y h y^t v−2y^{t+1}v=(λ−2(t+1))y^{t+1}v. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction proves the h formula for every t≥0. For x, the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=λv by H002 and H003. For t≥1 temporarily assume L2: xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. Discharging L2 proves the step, and induction gives the x formula for all t≥1. These identities are F001.

produces.statement: For every integer z1≥0, hy^z1 v=(λ−2z1)y^z1 v; for z1≥1, xy^z1 v=z1(λ−z1+1)y^{z1−1}v.

argument.text: For i∈I, iterating F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the product is 1 and this is v. All factors for i>0 are positive integers, and v≠0 by H003, so every e_i is nonzero over C. By F001, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i; these eigenvalues are distinct over C. To check independence, fix arbitrary coefficients c=(c_i)_{i∈I} and temporarily assume L3: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id) to this relation. It yields c_j∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0. The product, including an empty product, is nonzero, and e_j≠0, hence c_j=0. Discharge L3 to obtain independence. H002 gives dim_C V=n, and there are n independent e_i, so they form a complex basis. This proves F002.

produces.statement: The family (e_z1)_{z1∈I} is a complex basis of V; each e_z1 is nonzero, he_z1=(λ−2z1)e_z1, and dim_C V=n.

argument.text: F001 specialized to exponent λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if it is nonzero. Temporarily assume L4 that it is nonzero. Expanding it in the basis F002, the equality h y^{λ+1}v=(−λ−2)y^{λ+1}v forces every coefficient to vanish: for i∈I, (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i) is a nonzero complex scalar. This is a contradiction, so discharge L4 to conclude y^{λ+1}v=0. Applying further y powers gives all higher vanishing. F001 divided by i!, together with this termination and xv=0 from H003, gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. This proves F003.

produces.statement: y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers vanish. For z1∈I, xe_0=0 and xe_z1=(λ−z1+1)e_{z1−1} if z1≥1; ye_z1=(z1+1)e_{z1+1} if z1<λ and ye_λ=0; he_z1=(λ−2z1)e_z1.

argument.text: Iterate the displayed x,y matrices in F003 and divide by r!. For each natural r and i∈I with r≤i, x^r e_i/r!=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r}. If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed by x. For i+r≤λ, y^r e_i/r!=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r}; otherwise it passes the last vector and is zero. For r=0 the empty products are 1. These are precisely X_r,Y_r by definition. The displayed binomial coefficients, with nonnegative integer upper argument at least r, are integers. Together with F001–F003 this is every assertion of the asserted conclusion.

argument.text: H004 gives an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. By N001, dim_C V=n and |I|=n. Equality of the cardinalities of finite bases permits reindexing the given lattice basis by I. Thus there exists a family m=(m_i)_{i∈I} which is simultaneously a Z-basis of M and a complex basis of V. This is F001.

argument.text: Choose such a family m using F001. Since R is a commutative Z-algebra, M001 with A=Z, B=M, C0=R and d=m gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Its image under μ is the family m_i in V. A relation in its kernel is a finite R-linear relation among the complex-independent m_i, so all coefficients are zero. Thus μ is injective; the image is free of rank n and spans V over C. By H004, all X_r,Y_r preserve M, so their scalar extensions preserve M_R and μ intertwines them. Also x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=xy−yx preserves M because H002 gives [x,y]=h. This proves h-stability. Record F002: μ is injective with the claimed free, spanning and stability properties.

produces.statement: μ is injective; μ(M_R) is free of rank n over R and spans V over C; every X_z1 and Y_z1 preserves it. The operators x,y,h preserve M and extend to M_R and V_K.

argument.text: For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

argument.text: Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

argument.text: Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.

argument.text: Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. 12: /-!
13: # Quotienting out a free `ℤ`-module
14: 
15: If `G` is a rank `d` free `ℤ`-module, then `G/nG` is a finite group of cardinality `n ^ d`.
16: -/
17: 
18: @[expose] public section
19: 
20: open Finsupp Function Module
21: 
22: variable {G H M : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {n : ℕ}
23: 
24: variable (G n) in
25: /-- `ModN G n` denotes the quotient of `G` by multiples of `n` -/
26: abbrev ModN : Type _ := G ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
27: 
28: namespace ModN
29: 
30: instance : Module (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := QuotientAddGroup.zmodModule (by simp)
31: 
32: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
33: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of monoids: Monoid homomorphisms from `ModN G n`
34: are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
35: protected def liftEquiv [AddMonoid M] : (ModN G n →+ M) ≃ {φ : G →+ M // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} where
36:   toFun f := ⟨f.comp (QuotientAddGroup.mk' _), fun g ↦ by
37:     let Gn : AddSubgroup G := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).toAddSubgroup
38:     suffices n • g ∈ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn).ker by
39:       simp only [AddMonoidHom.coe_comp, comp_apply, ← map_nsmul]
40:       change f (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn (n • g)) = 0 -- Can we avoid `change`?
41:       rw [this, map_zero]
42:     simp [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk', Gn]⟩
43:   invFun φ := QuotientAddGroup.lift _ φ <| by rintro - ⟨g, rfl⟩; simpa using φ.property g
44:   left_inv f := by
45:     ext x
46:     induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on
47:     rfl -- Should `simp` suffice here?
48:   right_inv φ := by aesop
49: 
50: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of `ZMod n`-modules: `ZMod n`-linear maps from
51: `ModN G n` are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
52: protected def liftEquiv' [AddCommGroup H] [Module (ZMod n) H] :
53:     (ModN G n →ₗ[ZMod n] H) ≃ {φ : G →+ H // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} :=
54:   (AddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMapEquiv n).symm.toEquiv.trans ModN.liftEquiv
55: 
56: variable (n) in
57: /-- The quotient map `G → G / nG`. -/
58: def mkQ : G →+ ModN G n := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).mkQ
59: 
60: variable [NeZero n]
61: 
62: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
63: /-- Given a free module `G` over `ℤ`, construct the corresponding basis
64: of `G / ⟨n⟩` over `ℤ / nℤ`. -/
65: noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) : Basis ι (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := by
66:   set ψ : G →+ G := zsmulAddGroupHom n
67:   set nG := LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
68:   set H := G ⧸ nG
69:   set φ : G →ₗ[ℤ] H := nG.mkQ
70:   let mod : (ι →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := mapRange.linearMap (Int.castAddHom _).toIntLinearMap
71:   let f : G →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ℤ) := b.repr
72:   have hker : nG ≤ LinearMap.ker (mod.comp f) := by
73:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
74:     ext b
75:     simp [mod, f]
76:   let g : H →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := nG.liftQ (mod.comp f) hker
77:   refine ⟨.ofBijective (g.toAddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMap n) ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
78:   · rw [AddMonoidHom.coe_toZModLinearMap, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe, injective_iff_map_eq_zero,
79:       nG.mkQ_surjective.forall]
80:     intro x hx
81:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply, g] at hx
82:     rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply] at hx
83:     replace hx : ∀ b, ↑n ∣ f x b := by
84:       simpa [mod, DFunLike.ext_iff, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using! hx
85:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply]
86:     rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
87:     choose c hc using hx
88:     refine ⟨b.repr.symm ⟨(f x).support, c, by simp [hc, NeZero.ne]⟩, b.repr.injective ?_⟩
89:     simpa [DFunLike.ext_iff, eq_comm] using! hc
90:   · suffices mod ∘ b.repr = g ∘ nG.mkQ by
91:       exact (this ▸ (mapRange_surjective _ (map_zero _) ZMod.intCast_surjective).comp
92:         b.repr.surjective).of_comp
93:     ext x b
94:     simp [mod, g, f, H]
95: 
96: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
97: lemma basis_apply_eq_mkQ {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) (i : ι) : basis b i = mkQ n (b i) := by
98:   rw [Basis.apply_eq_iff]; simp [basis, mkQ]
99: 
100: variable [Module.Free ℤ G] [Module.Finite ℤ G]
101: 
102: instance instModuleFinite : Module.Finite (ZMod n) (ModN G n) :=
103:   .of_basis <| basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G
104: 
105: instance instFinite : Finite (ModN G n) := Module.finite_of_finite (ZMod n)
106: 
107: variable (G n)
108: @[simp] lemma natCard_eq : Nat.card (ModN G n) = n ^ Module.finrank ℤ G := by
109:   simp [Nat.card_congr (basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G).repr.toEquiv,
110:     Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Module.finrank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex]
111: 
112: end ModN

value.fact: If a complex vector space has finite dimension n and an indexed family consists of n linearly independent vectors, that family is a basis.

grounds.reason: V has finite complex dimension λ+1.
The finite index set I has n elements and n>0.
Before the basis conclusion, the polynomial isolation argument proves linear independence of the e_i.

value.justification: Choose a basis of n vectors, whose existence is part of finite dimension n, and express the given family as the columns of an n by n complex matrix. Independence says the homogeneous system has only the zero solution. Finite Gaussian elimination therefore has a pivot in every column and, since the matrix is square, every row. Thus every coordinate vector is a linear combination of the columns. The family spans and is independent, hence is a basis.

value.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1)/r!=binom(m,r) is an integer, with value 1 for r=0. Consequently the rising product (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer for integers a,r≥0.

grounds.reason: λ is a nonnegative integer.
i∈I means i is an integer with 0≤i≤λ.
r is an arbitrary natural number in S004.
For the x branch take a=λ−i≥0; for the y branch take a=i≥0. The respective products are exactly these rising products.

value.justification: On an m-element set the number of ordered r-tuples of distinct elements is m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1). Partition these tuples by their underlying r-element subset. Every class has r! elements, one for each ordering, so the quotient is the number of r-element subsets, the binomial coefficient. The empty tuple gives the r=0 case. Reversing the factors with m=a+r gives the rising-product identity.

value.fact: An integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of the finite-dimensional V can be reindexed by I when |I|=dim_C V=n.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies the simultaneous lattice and complex basis.
N001 supplies finite dimension n and |I|=n.

value.justification: Any basis of an n-dimensional vector space has n elements: the finite exchange argument bounds an independent family by the size of a spanning family, applied in both directions to two bases. A bijection between its index set and I then reindexes both basis properties without changing any vector.

value.fact: For a Z-linear endomorphism T of M, scalar extension to any commutative Z-algebra S is the S-linear endomorphism of S⊗_Z M determined by s⊗m↦s⊗T(m). For S=R and complex-linear T on V restricting to M, this extension intertwines μ with T. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v. Using [h,y]=−2y from H002, h y^{t+1}v=y h y^t v−2y^{t+1}v=(λ−2(t+1))y^{t+1}v. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction proves the h formula for every t≥0. For x, the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=λv by H002 and H003. For t≥1 temporarily assume L2: xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. Discharging L2 proves the step, and induction gives the x formula for all t≥1. These identities are F001.

For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

value.text: Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

produces.statement: J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C, every J_i equals J, and μ(M_R)=⊕_{aidx∈I}J e_aidx. There are R-linear coordinate maps coord_aidx:M_R→J and insertion maps ins_aidx:J→M_R. For u0∈M_R, μ(u0)=∑_{aidx∈I}coord_aidx(u0)e_aidx; for c0∈J, μ(ins_aidx(c0))=c0 e_aidx. The composite coord_aidx∘ins_bidx is zero when aidx≠bidx and the identity when aidx=bidx, and ∑_{aidx∈I}ins_aidx∘coord_aidx=Id.

value.text: Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.

produces.statement: Q is a localization of R at S_R; f:J→QJ is the R-linear inclusion, its target has compatible R- and Q-module structures, and it satisfies IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f). QJ is finite-dimensional over Q.

value.text: Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. In fraction language a zero image forces a zero numerator, since J⊂C is torsion-free. Define T_Q=Q⊗_R J and r=dim_Q T_Q. The isomorphism and F002 show this dimension is finite. Record F003.

produces.statement: Multiplication T_Q=Q⊗_R J→QJ⊂C is a Q-linear isomorphism onto QJ and injective into C. T_Q is finite-dimensional, with dimension r.

value.text: Set A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R. Instantiate the coordinate and insertion maps of F001, denoting them α_i and τ_i. Their scalar extensions give a Q-linear map A_Q→(T_Q)^I sending q⊗u to (q⊗α_i(u))_{i∈I}. Its inverse sends a tuple (z_i) to ∑_{i∈I}(1⊗τ_i)(z_i); here 1⊗τ_i denotes the tensor map q⊗c↦q⊗τ_i(c). These maps are well-defined by R-balancing. The equalities α_iτ_j=δ_ij Id and ∑τ_iα_i=Id in F001 verify the two composite identities, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus A_Q≅(T_Q)^I as Q-vector spaces. This proves F004.

produces.statement: A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R is Q-linearly isomorphic to the finite product (T_Q)^I by the coordinate tensor map and the sum of insertion tensor maps.

value.text: N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R with n elements. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R and C0=Q to this basis: its scalar extension is a Q-basis of A_Q with n elements, so dim_Q A_Q=n. Apply M003 with A=Q, index type I and constant module family T_Q. The field Q satisfies the strong rank condition by finite-dimensional linear algebra; I is finite with n elements by N001. By F003 each T_Q is finite-dimensional, hence free and finitely generated over Q. M003 gives dim_Q((T_Q)^I)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. F004 therefore gives n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, cancellation in the natural numbers yields r=1. F003 now gives dim_Q QJ=1, while F001 gives the finite generation, nonzero property and decomposition. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

value.text: H001 implies that every integer denominator prime to p maps to a nonzero element of K. Define ρ:R→K by ρ(a/b)=a_K b_K^{−1}. Cross multiplication makes this well-defined and a ring homomorphism extending Z→K. There is also the injective prime-field map F_p→K. Define Φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by Φ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c; its inverse is (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c. Both formulas respect the tensor relations (the R-action on K is through ρ), and the composites are identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Next define the map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K by u⊗c↦(u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends a residue tensor (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: replacing u by u+pt changes this by pt⊗c=t⊗pc=0. It is balanced over F_p, and its R-balancing is justified by R/pR≅F_p, explicitly a/b mod p↦a_p b_p^{-1}; the kernel is pR and every residue is obtained from an integer. These maps are inverse on generators. All maps commute with operators induced from M or M_R, by their formulas. Such x,y,h and divided powers exist by N002. This proves the natural identifications in F001.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K is the extension of Z→K, and there are natural K-linear operator-compatible isomorphisms V_K=M⊗_Z K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K. The first sends z1⊗z2 to (1⊗z1)⊗z2 and has inverse (z3⊗z1)⊗z2↦z1⊗ρ(z3)z2; the second sends z4⊗z2 to its residue tensor and its inverse is given by any representative z4.

value.text: Choose b as in N004. For each i∈I define m_i to be the unique μ-preimage of b e_i; N002 gives injectivity and N004 gives membership and the R-basis property of this family in M_R. Define β_i=Φ^{-1}(m_i⊗1)∈V_K. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R, C0=K, the algebra structure ρ and the R-basis (m_i). It gives the K-basis (1⊗m_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The factor-switching isomorphism c⊗u↦u⊗c (with inverse u⊗c↦c⊗u), followed by Φ^{-1}, gives the K-basis β. It has |I|=n=λ+1>0 elements by N001. Because μ intertwines the divided powers, and b is a common complex scalar, the matrices on m_i are exactly those on e_i from N001. F001 carries these matrices to V_K with every integer entry mapped into K. Thus xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The divided-power matrices also descend: X_r^K β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_{i−r} for r≤i, zero for r>i, and Y_r^K β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ, zero otherwise. Here X_r^K,Y_r^K denote the operators induced from X_r,Y_r on M_R. Record F002.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V_K indexed by I, with n=λ+1>0 elements and with the x,y,h matrices and all induced divided-power matrices stated in S002. Explicitly for z1∈I: xβ_0=0, xβ_z1=(λ−z1+1)β_{z1−1} (z1≥1), yβ_z1=(z1+1)β_{z1+1} (z1<λ), yβ_λ=0, hβ_z1=(λ−2z1)β_z1; X_z2^Kβ_z1=binom(λ−z1+z2,z2)β_{z1−z2} (z2≤z1) and zero otherwise; Y_z2^Kβ_z1=binom(z1+z2,z2)β_{z1+z2} (z1+z2≤λ) and zero otherwise, for every natural z2.

value.text: N002 gives, inside the localized lattice, E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}, with P0=Y_λX_λ, and says all these factors preserve it. In the basis (b e_i), E_ij has a single entry 1 in position (i,j), the same as in (e_i). Scalar extension through F001 therefore carries the equality to the operator T_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)^{-1})X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K on β, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K. It satisfies T_ijβ_k=β_i for k=j and 0 for k≠j. Since binom(λ,j) is a unit of R by N002, its image is a unit of K (ρ sends its inverse to an inverse). Also for 0≤r≤λ<p, no factor of r! is divisible by p by H001, so r! maps to a nonzero element of K. The equalities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold over C by definition, hence on M_R by injectivity of μ, and after scalar extension. Consequently X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. This proves F003.

produces.statement: For every z1,z2,z3∈I, T_{z1,z2}=binom(λ,z2)_K^{-1}X_{λ−z1}^K P_K Y_{λ−z2}^K, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K, and T_{z1,z2}β_z3=β_z1 if z3=z2 and zero otherwise. All these binomial coefficient inverses exist in K. For every natural z4 with 0≤z4≤λ, z4!_K≠0 and X_z4^K=(z4!_K)^{-1}x^z4, Y_z4^K=(z4!_K)^{-1}y^z4.

value.text: Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x and y. Induction on the power shows it is invariant under x^r and y^r for every natural r. Because W is K-linear it is stable under scalar multiples and compositions of its preserving operators. F003 expresses all X_r^K,Y_r^K for r≤λ as scalar multiples of these powers, and T_ij as a scalar times a composition of these operators, since λ−i,λ,λ−j are all in [0,λ]. Therefore W is invariant under every T_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with F001–F003, existentially quantify the compatible basis β to obtain the asserted conclusion.

By classical cases, either W={0}, which is already one required alternative, or temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. Under L1,L2, a nonzero vector in W has a unique expansion in the basis β; at least one coefficient is nonzero, since a vector with every coefficient zero is zero. value.text: F001 proves nonzero dimension and F003 proves exactly the required subspace assertion. L_K is spanned over K by the three induced generators x,y,h, so a K-linear subspace is L_K-invariant exactly when it is invariant under those three operators. Thus these assertions are irreducibility of V(K) as an L(K)-module. The original H001 allows λ=0: then I={0}, every relevant factorial and binomial coefficient is 1, and N005 gives the same one-dimensional conclusion. If p=2 the allowed λ are 0 and 1; N005's matrix-unit argument still applies, with no use of distinct h-eigenvalues in K. Nothing used algebraic closure of K. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

value.text: For i∈I, iterating F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the product is 1 and this is v. All factors for i>0 are positive integers, and v≠0 by H003, so every e_i is nonzero over C. By F001, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i; these eigenvalues are distinct over C. To check independence, fix arbitrary coefficients c=(c_i)_{i∈I} and temporarily assume L3: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id) to this relation. It yields c_j∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0. The product, including an empty product, is nonzero, and e_j≠0, hence c_j=0. Discharge L3 to obtain independence. H002 gives dim_C V=n, and there are n independent e_i, so they form a complex basis. This proves F002.

F001 specialized to exponent λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if it is nonzero. Temporarily assume L4 that it is nonzero. Expanding it in the basis F002, the equality h y^{λ+1}v=(−λ−2)y^{λ+1}v forces every coefficient to vanish: for i∈I, (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i) is a nonzero complex scalar. This is a contradiction, so discharge L4 to conclude y^{λ+1}v=0. Applying further y powers gives all higher vanishing. F001 divided by i!, together with this termination and xv=0 from H003, gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. This proves F003.

Iterate the displayed x,y matrices in F003 and divide by r!. For each natural r and i∈I with r≤i, x^r e_i/r!=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r}. If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed by x. For i+r≤λ, y^r e_i/r!=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r}; otherwise it passes the last vector and is zero. For r=0 the empty products are 1. These are precisely X_r,Y_r by definition. The displayed binomial coefficients, with nonnegative integer upper argument at least r, are integers. Together with F001–F003 this is every assertion of the asserted conclusion.

H004 gives an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. By N001, dim_C V=n and |I|=n. Equality of the cardinalities of finite bases permits reindexing the given lattice basis by I. Thus there exists a family m=(m_i)_{i∈I} which is simultaneously a Z-basis of M and a complex basis of V. This is F001.

Choose such a family m using F001. Since R is a commutative Z-algebra, M001 with A=Z, B=M, C0=R and d=m gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Its image under μ is the family m_i in V. A relation in its kernel is a finite R-linear relation among the complex-independent m_i, so all coefficients are zero. Thus μ is injective; the image is free of rank n and spans V over C. By H004, all X_r,Y_r preserve M, so their scalar extensions preserve M_R and μ intertwines them. Also x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=xy−yx preserves M because H002 gives [x,y]=h. This proves h-stability. Record F002: μ is injective with the claimed free, spanning and stability properties.

For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.
