79: variable [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M']

81: variable (ι R M) in
82: /-- A `Basis ι R M` for a module `M` is the type of `ι`-indexed `R`-bases of `M`.
83: 
84: The basis vectors are available as `DFunLike.coe (b : Basis ι R M) : ι → M`.
85: To turn a linear independent family of vectors spanning `M` into a basis, use `Basis.mk`.
86: They are internally represented as linear equivs `M ≃ₗ[R] (ι →₀ R)`,
87: available as `Basis.repr`.
88: -/
89: @[wikidata Q189569]
90: structure Basis where
91:   /-- `Basis.ofRepr` constructs a basis given an assignment of coordinates to each vector. -/
92:   ofRepr ::
93:     /-- `repr` is the linear equivalence sending a vector `x` to its coordinates:
94:     the `c`s such that `x = ∑ i, c i`. -/
95:     repr : M ≃ₗ[R] ι →₀ R
96: 
97: namespace Basis
98: 
99: instance : Inhabited (Basis ι R (ι →₀ R)) :=
100:   ⟨.ofRepr (LinearEquiv.refl _ _)⟩
101: 
102: variable (b b₁ : Basis ι R M) (i : ι) (c : R) (x : M)
103: 
104: section repr
105: 
106: theorem repr_injective : Injective (repr : Basis ι R M → M ≃ₗ[R] ι →₀ R) := fun f g h => by
107:   cases f; cases g; congr
108: 
109: /-- `b i` is the `i`th basis vector. -/
110: instance instFunLike : FunLike (Basis ι R M) ι M where
111:   coe b i := b.repr.symm (Finsupp.single i 1)
112:   coe_injective f g h := repr_injective <| LinearEquiv.symm_bijective.injective <|
113:     LinearEquiv.toLinearMap_injective <| by ext; exact congr_fun h _
114: 
115: @[simp]
116: theorem coe_ofRepr (e : M ≃ₗ[R] ι →₀ R) : ⇑(ofRepr e) = fun i => e.symm (Finsupp.single i 1) :=
117:   rfl
118: 
119: protected theorem injective [Nontrivial R] : Injective b :=
120:   b.repr.symm.injective.comp fun _ _ => (Finsupp.single_left_inj (one_ne_zero : (1 : R) ≠ 0)).mp
121: 
122: theorem repr_symm_single_one : b.repr.symm (Finsupp.single i 1) = b i :=
123:   rfl

656: section Coord
657: 
658: variable (i : ι)
659: 
660: /-- `b.coord i` is the linear function giving the `i`-th coordinate of a vector
661: with respect to the basis `b`.
662: 
663: `b.coord i` is an element of the dual space. In particular, for
664: finite-dimensional spaces it is the `ι`th basis vector of the dual space.
665: -/
666: @[simps!]
667: def coord : M →ₗ[R] R :=
668:   Finsupp.lapply i ∘ₗ ↑b.repr
669: 
670: theorem forall_coord_eq_zero_iff {x : M} : (∀ i, b.coord i x = 0) ↔ x = 0 :=
671:   Iff.trans (by simp only [b.coord_apply, DFunLike.ext_iff, Finsupp.zero_apply])
672:     b.repr.map_eq_zero_iff
673: 
674: /-- The sum of the coordinates of an element `m : M` with respect to a basis. -/
675: noncomputable def sumCoords : M →ₗ[R] R :=
676:   (Finsupp.lsum ℕ fun _ => LinearMap.id) ∘ₗ (b.repr : M →ₗ[R] ι →₀ R)
677: 
678: @[simp]
679: theorem coe_sumCoords : (b.sumCoords : M → R) = fun m => (b.repr m).sum fun _ => id :=
680:   rfl
681: 
682: @[simp high]
683: theorem coe_sumCoords_of_fintype [Fintype ι] : (b.sumCoords : M → R) = ∑ i, b.coord i := by
684:   ext m
685:   simp only [sumCoords, Finsupp.sum_fintype, LinearMap.id_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, coord_apply,
686:     id, Fintype.sum_apply, imp_true_iff, Finsupp.coe_lsum, LinearMap.coe_comp, comp_apply,
687:     LinearMap.coe_sum]
688: 
689: @[simp]
690: theorem sumCoords_self_apply : b.sumCoords (b i) = 1 := by
691:   simp only [Basis.sumCoords, LinearMap.id_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, id, Basis.repr_self,
692:     Function.comp_apply, Finsupp.coe_lsum, LinearMap.coe_comp, Finsupp.sum_single_index]
693: 
694: theorem dvd_coord_smul (i : ι) (m : M) (r : R) : r ∣ b.coord i (r • m) :=
695:   ⟨b.coord i m, by simp⟩
696: 
697: theorem coord_repr_symm (b : Basis ι R M) (i : ι) (f : ι →₀ R) :
698:     b.coord i (b.repr.symm f) = f i := by
699:   simp only [repr_symm_apply, coord_apply, repr_linearCombination]

200: @[simp]
201: theorem comp_codLift :
202:     p.comp (f.codLift p hp h) = f := by

209: def restrict (f : M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) {p : Submodule R M} {q : Submodule R₂ M₂} (hf : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ q) :
210:     p →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] q :=

215:     (hf : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ q) (x : p) : ↑(f.restrict hf x) = f x :=

220:     (hf : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ q) (x : p) : ↑(f.restrict hf x) = f x :=

224:     (hf : ∀ x ∈ p, f x ∈ q) (x : p) : f.restrict hf x = ⟨f x, hf x.1 x.2⟩ :=

value.text: Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. In fraction language a zero image forces a zero numerator, since J⊂C is torsion-free. Define T_Q=Q⊗_R J and r=dim_Q T_Q. The isomorphism and F002 show this dimension is finite. Record F003.

Set A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R. Instantiate the coordinate and insertion maps of F001, denoting them α_i and τ_i. Their scalar extensions give a Q-linear map A_Q→(T_Q)^I sending q⊗u to (q⊗α_i(u))_{i∈I}. Its inverse sends a tuple (z_i) to ∑_{i∈I}(1⊗τ_i)(z_i); here 1⊗τ_i denotes the tensor map q⊗c↦q⊗τ_i(c). These maps are well-defined by R-balancing. The equalities α_iτ_j=δ_ij Id and ∑τ_iα_i=Id in F001 verify the two composite identities, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus A_Q≅(T_Q)^I as Q-vector spaces. This proves F004.

N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R with n elements. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R and C0=Q to this basis: its scalar extension is a Q-basis of A_Q with n elements, so dim_Q A_Q=n. Apply M003 with A=Q, index type I and constant module family T_Q. The field Q satisfies the strong rank condition by finite-dimensional linear algebra; I is finite with n elements by N001. By F003 each T_Q is finite-dimensional, hence free and finitely generated over Q. M003 gives dim_Q((T_Q)^I)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. F004 therefore gives n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, cancellation in the natural numbers yields r=1. F003 now gives dim_Q QJ=1, while F001 gives the finite generation, nonzero property and decomposition. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

Choose 0≠a∈J using N003. N003 identifies Q⊗_R J with the one-dimensional subspace QJ⊂C. Since a≠0, a is a Q-basis of that line. Take finite generators of J, discard any zero generators, and use J≠0 to see the remaining list is nonempty. Every remaining generator is a nonzero rational multiple of a. Therefore there exist k≥1 and q_1,…,q_k∈Q\{0} such that J is generated over R by q_1a,…,q_ka. This is F001.

Choose k,q as in F001. For each 1≤j≤k, write q_j as a ratio of nonzero integers, remove the maximal powers of the prime p from numerator and denominator, and define ν_j to be the difference of these two exponents. Then q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a rational whose numerator and denominator are both prime to p. Such u_j and its reciprocal belong to R, so u_j is a unit. This construction also covers negative ν_j. Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j and b=p^ν a. The minimum exists and is attained because k≥1 and the list is finite. All q_j a belong to Rb, since q_j a=p^{ν_j−ν}u_j b and ν_j−ν≥0. Also b≠0, since p is prime by H001 and a≠0. Record F002, including the existence of a minimizing index.

Choose a minimizing index j0 from F002. Then q_{j0}a=u_{j0}b, and u_{j0} is an R-unit. Since q_{j0}a is a generator of J by F001, b=u_{j0}^{−1}q_{j0}a belongs to J and Rb⊆J. The reverse inclusion follows from F001 and the inclusion of every generator in Rb from F002. Thus J=Rb with b∈J nonzero. This is F003.

Substitute F003 in the direct decomposition of N003 to obtain μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}R(b e_i). The vectors b e_i are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex-independent by N001. They span by the displayed decomposition, so are an R-basis. Since μ is injective by N002, their unique preimages form an R-basis of M_R. Existentially quantify b to prove the asserted conclusion. In particular no rank-one claim has been inferred from containment in C alone.

H001 implies that every integer denominator prime to p maps to a nonzero element of K. Define ρ:R→K by ρ(a/b)=a_K b_K^{−1}. Cross multiplication makes this well-defined and a ring homomorphism extending Z→K. There is also the injective prime-field map F_p→K. Define Φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by Φ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c; its inverse is (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c. Both formulas respect the tensor relations (the R-action on K is through ρ), and the composites are identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Next define the map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K by u⊗c↦(u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends a residue tensor (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: replacing u by u+pt changes this by pt⊗c=t⊗pc=0. It is balanced over F_p, and its R-balancing is justified by R/pR≅F_p, explicitly a/b mod p↦a_p b_p^{-1}; the kernel is pR and every residue is obtained from an integer. These maps are inverse on generators. All maps commute with operators induced from M or M_R, by their formulas. Such x,y,h and divided powers exist by N002. This proves the natural identifications in F001.

value.text: Choose b as in N004. For each i∈I define m_i to be the unique μ-preimage of b e_i; N002 gives injectivity and N004 gives membership and the R-basis property of this family in M_R. Define β_i=Φ^{-1}(m_i⊗1)∈V_K. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R, C0=K, the algebra structure ρ and the R-basis (m_i). It gives the K-basis (1⊗m_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The factor-switching isomorphism c⊗u↦u⊗c (with inverse u⊗c↦c⊗u), followed by Φ^{-1}, gives the K-basis β. It has |I|=n=λ+1>0 elements by N001. Because μ intertwines the divided powers, and b is a common complex scalar, the matrices on m_i are exactly those on e_i from N001. F001 carries these matrices to V_K with every integer entry mapped into K. Thus xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The divided-power matrices also descend: X_r^K β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_{i−r} for r≤i, zero for r>i, and Y_r^K β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ, zero otherwise. Here X_r^K,Y_r^K denote the operators induced from X_r,Y_r on M_R. Record F002.

N002 gives, inside the localized lattice, E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}, with P0=Y_λX_λ, and says all these factors preserve it. In the basis (b e_i), E_ij has a single entry 1 in position (i,j), the same as in (e_i). Scalar extension through F001 therefore carries the equality to the operator T_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)^{-1})X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K on β, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K. It satisfies T_ijβ_k=β_i for k=j and 0 for k≠j. Since binom(λ,j) is a unit of R by N002, its image is a unit of K (ρ sends its inverse to an inverse). Also for 0≤r≤λ<p, no factor of r! is divisible by p by H001, so r! maps to a nonzero element of K. The equalities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold over C by definition, hence on M_R by injectivity of μ, and after scalar extension. Consequently X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. This proves F003.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x and y. Induction on the power shows it is invariant under x^r and y^r for every natural r. Because W is K-linear it is stable under scalar multiples and compositions of its preserving operators. F003 expresses all X_r^K,Y_r^K for r≤λ as scalar multiples of these powers, and T_ij as a scalar times a composition of these operators, since λ−i,λ,λ−j are all in [0,λ]. Therefore W is invariant under every T_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with F001–F003, existentially quantify the compatible basis β to obtain the asserted conclusion.

Choose a basis β and the compatible matrix operators guaranteed by N005. This basis has n=λ+1>0 elements, so dim_K V_K=n>0 and V_K≠0; record this as F001. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is x,y-invariant, and N005 says it is invariant under every T_ij. By classical cases, either W={0}, which is already one required alternative, or temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. Under L1,L2, a nonzero vector in W has a unique expansion in the basis β; at least one coefficient is nonzero, since a vector with every coefficient zero is zero. Thus there exist w∈W, a coefficient family c:I→K, and j∈I with w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i≠0 and c_j≠0. This is F002 under L1,L2.

Choose w,c,j as in F002. For every i∈I, linearity and the matrix-unit action in N005 give T_ij w=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiply by c_j^{-1} to get β_i∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine this result with the W={0} case to obtain W={0} or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 to get the implication for this arbitrary W, then universally quantify W. This gives F003 with no remaining local assumptions.

R001.fact: If a complex vector space has finite dimension n and an indexed family consists of n linearly independent vectors, that family is a basis.

grounds.reason: V has finite complex dimension λ+1.
The finite index set I has n elements and n>0.
Before the basis conclusion, the polynomial isolation argument proves linear independence of the e_i.

R001.justification: Choose a basis of n vectors, whose existence is part of finite dimension n, and express the given family as the columns of an n by n complex matrix. Independence says the homogeneous system has only the zero solution. Finite Gaussian elimination therefore has a pivot in every column and, since the matrix is square, every row. Thus every coordinate vector is a linear combination of the columns. The family spans and is independent, hence is a basis.

R001.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1)/r!=binom(m,r) is an integer, with value 1 for r=0. Consequently the rising product (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer for integers a,r≥0.

grounds.reason: λ is a nonnegative integer.
i∈I means i is an integer with 0≤i≤λ.
r is an arbitrary natural number in S004.
For the x branch take a=λ−i≥0; for the y branch take a=i≥0. The respective products are exactly these rising products.

R001.justification: On an m-element set the number of ordered r-tuples of distinct elements is m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1). Partition these tuples by their underlying r-element subset. Every class has r! elements, one for each ordering, so the quotient is the number of r-element subsets, the binomial coefficient. The empty tuple gives the r=0 case. Reversing the factors with m=a+r gives the rising-product identity.

R002.fact: An integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of the finite-dimensional V can be reindexed by I when |I|=dim_C V=n.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies the simultaneous lattice and complex basis.
N001 supplies finite dimension n and |I|=n.

R002.justification: Any basis of an n-dimensional vector space has n elements: the finite exchange argument bounds an independent family by the size of a spanning family, applied in both directions to two bases. A bijection between its index set and I then reindexes both basis properties without changing any vector.

R002.fact: For a Z-linear endomorphism T of M, scalar extension to any commutative Z-algebra S is the S-linear endomorphism of S⊗_Z M determined by s⊗m↦s⊗T(m). For S=R and complex-linear T on V restricting to M, this extension intertwines μ with T. An injective R-linear map carrying an R-basis to a complex basis identifies its image as a free R-module of that rank spanning V.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies preservation of M by every divided power.
H002 supplies h=xy−yx, so h also preserves M after x=X_1 and y=Y_1.
R is viewed inside C.
μ(r⊗m)=rm.
V_K=M⊗_Z K; K is a commutative Z-algebra as a field.
M001 has provided the tensor basis, whose images are the complex basis chosen from F001.

R002.justification: The displayed pure-tensor formula respects additivity and integer balancing because T is Z-linear; hence it descends to the tensor product. Equality with Tμ holds on pure tensors and therefore on their finite sums. Every kernel vector has a finite expansion in the tensor basis; its images give a complex-linear relation, so all R-coefficients vanish since R embeds in C. The images of the basis then freely generate the image and span V over C. The same tensor construction with M⊗_Z K gives the asserted K-linear induced operators.

R002.fact: If p is prime and 0≤j≤λ<p, then p does not divide binom(λ,j), and binom(λ,j) is a unit of R=Z_(p).

grounds.reason: p is prime and 0≤λ<p.
j∈I means 0≤j≤λ.
A rational with denominator prime to p lies in R.

R002.justification: Every positive factor in λ! lies strictly between 0 and p. Reduction modulo p is in the field Z/pZ, so the product of these nonzero residues is nonzero; the empty product for λ=0 is 1. The integer identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! then rules out p dividing binom(λ,j). Its rational reciprocal belongs to R and multiplies it to 1.

R003.fact: If g_1,...,g_m generate J as an R-module and R⊂Q, then g_1,...,g_m span QJ=span_Q J over Q. In particular QJ has finite dimension.

grounds.reason: F001 proves finite generation of J.
R is the specified subring of Q.
QJ is the rational span of J.

R003.justification: Every element of J is an R-linear combination of the generators, hence a rational combination. Substituting into a finite rational combination proves the spanning assertion. Successively discard each generator lying in the span of its predecessors; the retained finite list is independent and still spans, hence is a finite basis.

R003.fact: For an R-linear map g:U→W and a commutative R-algebra Q, the balanced rule q⊗u↦q⊗g(u) defines a Q-linear map Q⊗_R U→Q⊗_R W. Such tensor products are generated over Q by pure tensors, so two Q-linear maps agreeing on pure tensors agree everywhere.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies R-linear coordinate and insertion maps with both composite identities.
S004 uses these maps between M_R and J and takes finite sums indexed by I.
R⊂Q supplies the algebra structure.
I is finite.

R003.justification: The proposed rule is additive in each factor and respects (qa)⊗u=q⊗(au) because g(au)=ag(u); the tensor universal property supplies the map. A tensor product is constructed from finite sums of pure tensors modulo the bilinearity and balancing relations. Consequently checking each composite on pure tensors and extending by linearity proves S004's inverse identities.

R003.fact: A vector space over Q with a finite spanning set has a finite basis; the cardinality of any finite basis is its dimension, and a linear isomorphism preserves that dimension. Moreover an injective Q-linear map Q^a→Q^b forces a≤b, so Q satisfies the strong rank condition required by M003.

grounds.reason: F002 establishes finite-dimensional QJ.
F003 identifies T_Q with QJ and establishes its finite dimension.
F004 is a Q-linear isomorphism from A_Q to (T_Q)^I.
N002 supplies a free R-module of rank n.
M001 supplies the scalar-extended Q-basis.

R003.justification: Pruning a finite spanning list gives a basis. Gaussian elimination over a field shows that an independent list in the span of b vectors has at most b members: each pivot uses a distinct one of the b rows. Applying this in both directions to finite bases proves equality of their sizes. An isomorphism carries a basis to a basis. Under an injection Q^a→Q^b, the images of the a standard basis vectors are independent, so elimination yields a≤b. Finite bases also directly establish freeness and finite generation used in M003.

R004.fact: If L is a one-dimensional Q-subspace of C, 0 != a belongs to L, and a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of L is given, then J has a finite nonempty generating list q_1 a,...,q_k a with each q_j a nonzero and each q_j in Q\{0}.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated and dim_Q QJ=1.
QJ is the rational span of J, so J is contained in QJ.
a is chosen nonzero in J.

R004.justification: A nonzero vector in a one-dimensional vector space spans it: relative to any one-element basis, its coefficient is nonzero and can be inverted. Express each member of a finite generating list in this basis a. Removing zero members preserves the generated submodule and cannot remove all members since J is nonzero. The surviving rational coefficients are nonzero.

R004.fact: For a positive prime integer p and any nonzero rational q, there are nu in Z and u in Q with q=p^nu u and both u and u^(-1) in Z_(p). A finite nonempty list of such integer exponents has an attained minimum.

grounds.reason: p is prime, hence p>=2.
F001 gives finitely many nonzero rational coefficients with positive list length.
R consists of rational fractions whose denominator is not divisible by p.

R004.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. For each nonzero integer m, the exponents e>=0 for which p^e divides m form a nonempty finite set: divisibility implies p^e<=|m| and p>=2 bounds e. Choose its largest exponent. Thus A=p^alpha A' and B=p^beta B', with neither A' nor B' divisible by p. Set nu=alpha-beta and u=A'/B'. Both u and its reciprocal have allowed denominators in R, so u is an R-unit. Negative nu causes no problem in Q. Comparing finitely many integer entries recursively yields an entry realizing their minimum. This is the factorization and minimum construction already used in S002.

R004.fact: If R is a subring of C, (e_i) is a finite C-linearly independent family, b is a nonzero complex scalar and L is the internal sum of R(b e_i), then (b e_i) is an R-basis of L. If mu:T->V is R-linear, injective and has image L, the unique preimages of this family form an R-basis of T.

grounds.reason: R is viewed as a subring of C.
The e_i form a complex basis.

R004.justification: In a finite relation sum_i r_i b e_i=0, complex independence gives r_i b=0 for every i. Since b is nonzero, every r_i=0 in C and hence in R. The displayed sum supplies spanning. R005.fact: For modules over a commutative ring, an additive balanced map on pairs determines a unique linear map out of their tensor product. Pure tensors generate additively, so two linear maps agreeing on all pure tensors agree everywhere; inverse compositions checked on pure tensors give inverse linear maps.

R006.fact: For a finite K-basis (β_i) indexed by I, dim_K V_K=|I| and each vector has a unique expansion ∑_{i∈I}c_iβ_i. If |I|>0 then V_K≠0. If a K-subspace W≠{0}, it contains a nonzero vector whose basis expansion has at least one nonzero coefficient.

R006.justification: Spanning gives a finite expansion and linear independence gives uniqueness. A nonempty independent family contains a nonzero vector, and the finite basis cardinality is its dimension. A subspace contains zero, so inequality with {0} supplies a nonzero member. An expansion with all coefficients zero is zero, hence a nonzero member has a nonzero coefficient.

R006.fact: For L_K=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K with the specified K-linear action, x,y,h span L_K over K. A K-linear subspace of V_K is invariant under L_K if and only if it is invariant under those three operators.

grounds.reason: D016 defines L_K as this tensor product and specifies its induced action and generator tensors.
N005 supplies the induced operators on V_K.

R006.justification: Elements of a tensor product are finite sums of pure tensors. Write each first factor as ax+by+ch with integers a,b,c; tensor bilinearity expresses each pure tensor as a K-linear combination of x⊗1,y⊗1,h⊗1. Invariance under the generators therefore implies invariance under each Lie algebra element by linearity of the action and subspace closure. The converse follows by taking each generator.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
59: 
60: Checked auxiliary propositions receive a `yui_aux_...` name and an explicit
61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual
63: proof bodies and compiles them into standalone assembly. They are same-node
64: implementation lemmas, not extra assumptions. Read the helper index after a
65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66: 
67: Separate diagnostic printing from proving. `show_term` and similar suggestion
68: output may spend substantial time after the proof tactic runs. If that diagnostic
69: wrapper is implicated, check the same proof without it; only the new successful
70: check establishes acceptance. Do not ignore an unsuccessful process exit. If
71: small helpers pass but a monolithic body exhausts resources, retain the separate
72: checked helper declarations and compose them rather than repeatedly copying
73: their bodies into a growing proof.

Choose the finite nonempty length k from F001.
Choose the rational generator coefficients from F001.
Define ν_j by removing p-powers from the numerator and denominator of q_j.
Define u_j=p^{−ν_j}q_j.
Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j.
Define b=p^ν a.
Choose j0 with ν_{j0}=ν using F002.

argument.text: Choose 0≠a∈J using N003. N003 identifies Q⊗_R J with the one-dimensional subspace QJ⊂C. Since a≠0, a is a Q-basis of that line. Take finite generators of J, discard any zero generators, and use J≠0 to see the remaining list is nonempty. Every remaining generator is a nonzero rational multiple of a. Therefore there exist k≥1 and q_1,…,q_k∈Q\{0} such that J is generated over R by q_1a,…,q_ka. This is F001.

produces.statement: There exist z1≥1 and a family z2 indexed by {1,…,z1} of nonzero rational numbers such that J=∑_{j=1}^z1 R(z2_j a).

argument.text: Choose k,q as in F001. For each 1≤j≤k, write q_j as a ratio of nonzero integers, remove the maximal powers of the prime p from numerator and denominator, and define ν_j to be the difference of these two exponents. Then q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a rational whose numerator and denominator are both prime to p. Such u_j and its reciprocal belong to R, so u_j is a unit. This construction also covers negative ν_j. Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j and b=p^ν a. The minimum exists and is attained because k≥1 and the list is finite. All q_j a belong to Rb, since q_j a=p^{ν_j−ν}u_j b and ν_j−ν≥0. Also b≠0, since p is prime by H001 and a≠0. Record F002, including the existence of a minimizing index.

produces.statement: b=p^ν a≠0, every q_z1 a belongs to Rb, each u_z1 is a unit of R with q_z1=p^{ν_z1}u_z1, and there exists z2∈{1,…,k} with ν_{z2}=ν.

argument.text: Choose a minimizing index j0 from F002. Then q_{j0}a=u_{j0}b, and u_{j0} is an R-unit. Since q_{j0}a is a generator of J by F001, b=u_{j0}^{−1}q_{j0}a belongs to J and Rb⊆J. The reverse inclusion follows from F001 and the inclusion of every generator in Rb from F002. Thus J=Rb with b∈J nonzero. This is F003.

produces.statement: b∈J, b≠0, and J=Rb.

argument.text: Substitute F003 in the direct decomposition of N003 to obtain μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}R(b e_i). The vectors b e_i are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex-independent by N001. They span by the displayed decomposition, so are an R-basis. Since μ is injective by N002, their unique preimages form an R-basis of M_R. Existentially quantify b to prove the asserted conclusion. In particular no rank-one claim has been inferred from containment in C alone.

source_route_and_coverage.notes: Read the complete frozen source, specification, source map, contract, plan, background supplement, signature file and type result, with the minimal-translation and relevant Audit B/Lean safeguards. All 23 source paragraphs are represented: T001-T004 cover S001-S004 (commutator induction, polynomial eigenvalue isolation, dimension, termination and integral divided-power formulas); T005-T006 cover S005-S007 (the arbitrary lattice, localization and matrix units); T007-T010 cover S008-S012 (coordinate modules, actual rational multiplication map, tensor coordinate equivalence and n=nr); T011-T012 cover S013-S016 (minimal p-exponent and common-scalar lattice basis); T013-T014 cover S017-S020 (natural reduction maps, transported matrices and stability); T015 covers S021-S023 (nonzero dimension and matrix-unit irreducibility). N001-N005 are retained in T004,T006,T010,T012,T014 respectively, and T015 is the complete source P. In particular rank one is obtained by rational dimension cancellation, and the standard-shaped localized basis is proved for the arbitrary input lattice. No alternate proof route or additional project hypothesis is introduced.

parameters_and_allowed_inputs.notes: There are no original external E inputs. The complete P signature has exactly the proposed global data and H001-H004, with no internal T hypothesis retained. Nat p represents the source positive integer prime; ell remains integer with both 0≤ell and ell<p. Field K and CharP K p impose neither algebraic closure nor p>2. H002 retains finite complex dimension ell+1, the three commutators, highest-vector existence and complex irreducibility; together with H003 it is equivalent to the source representation data: assigning the Chevalley basis to the three operators gives the sl2(C) action, and invariance under these operators is invariance under that action. H004 retains an arbitrary simultaneous integer/complex basis, with existential finite indexing, and all natural divided powers preserve M; closure under the generated integer algebra is equivalent to this generator stability. This does not assume a string basis for M. Checked helper inputs against all six direct boundaries: T001-T004 use only R001 inputs; T005-T006 use R002 inputs and produced N001; T007-T010 use R003 inputs and earlier same-node helpers; T011-T012 use R004 inputs and their own principality helper; T013-T014 use R005 inputs and their own reduction helper; T015 uses precisely H001 and produced N005. All internal hypotheses have earlier producers in this acyclic plan. Mathlib is freely available; its registration/names were not audited.

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Verified the correspondence claims in both directions for the actual objects and scalar fields. A Z-submodule of the complex vector space is exactly an additive subgroup with its canonical integer action. Fin(ell.toNat+1) includes both integer endpoints under H001; all natural subtractions in the action formulas occur in guarded in-range branches. R is the concrete subalgebra of Q generated by allowed denominator inverses; T005 explicitly requires its two-way fraction description, injectivity of the actual mu, a finite R-basis, complex spanning, lattice preservation and divided-power intertwining. In the pinned library liftBaseChange sends a⊗m to a•f(m), so mu/muR are scalar multiplication, J is exactly the inverse image of that range under c↦c e_i, and qmul is the actual multiplication into C. T008 requires both its injectivity and exact range QJ, while T010 requires finite rational dimensions and rank one; no dimension over C is substituted. T012 explicitly supplies a common nonzero complex scalar, the image decomposition and an R-basis of MR with unique mu-preimages. VK=K⊗Z M identifies with the source M⊗Z K by the canonical tensor flip, which also intertwines induced maps. T013's reductions predicate requires genuine K-linear equivalences with natural pure-tensor formulas, not just named isomorphism claims: the pinned ModN G p is G modulo the range of multiplication by p, and ZMod.algebra K p is the canonical characteristic-p algebra. The pinned baseChange applies f on the lattice factor; latticeOp's preservation branch is actual restriction, and preservation/intertwining is supplied by H004 and T005, not silently assumed by the definition.
